title: How Forward Deployed Engineering is done at Cognition — Jia Wu
talk_summary: A Cognition deployed-engineering lead describes how they embed engineers with customers to map agent capabilities onto the highest-leverage business problems, then feed field learnings back into product. The concrete transferable ideas are outcome-based measurement of agent sessions, mapping agent work to the SDLC bottleneck (test/review/deploy, not coding), and event-triggered automations instead of manual agent invocation.

takeaways.technique: Map agents to the SDLC bottleneck, not to coding
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly treat coding as mostly solved and target the surrounding steps (testing, review, deploy, maintain) where the real cost and delay live, mapping agent capabilities to those steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the problem isn't like writing code faster, that's usually only 20% of the problem. The problem really just becomes like how do you test this code? How do you review and deploy this code?

takeaways.technique: Event-triggered automations instead of manual agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They set up agents to respond to specific alerts and events so humans don't manually trigger runs; the agent runs the automation itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we set up the agent in a way that it runs all of the automations for us... It can respond to like specific alerts, specific events.

takeaways.technique: Outcome metrics per agent session (productive vs total hours)
takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument each agent session/trajectory and derive how many engineering hours were generated versus actually productive, plus PR counts and timeline compression, to prove value rather than token spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have metrics that allow you to derive how many engineering hours you can actually generate and how much how many engineering hours are actually productive
takeaways.numbers: ~150% headcount equivalent over 3 months; 82% delivery timeline reduction; ~2x PRs vs single-point tools

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly moved the KPI from maximizing token usage to measurable delivery outcomes, because customers now ask whether they get true value or just burn tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the target or KPI for whatever deployed engineers were trying to do is maximize token usage... now, the problem has really shifted into the delivery space

takeaways.technique: Field feedback as highest-fidelity eval set
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat real customer problems as the highest-fidelity evaluation set and route recurring failure shapes back into product as features or fixes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have the highest fidelity evaluation set that comes back from our customers

takeaways.technique: Relentless 'why' triage of work before automating
takeaways.what_they_do: Before deploying agents they ask why a problem matters to the business and whether it's common across the org or a one-off, to avoid automating low-leverage work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we always ask ourselves, "Why are we solving this problem? Does this problem matter to the to the business as a whole?"
